as_told.title: Geological paper on hydrocarbon seepages under Giza

plain: This story is about what lies under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand. A researcher, Geoffrey Drumm, says a scientific paper shows a karst system beneath the plateau, meaning caves and tunnels hollowed out of the rock. According to him, this system is the source of hydrogen sulfide, a smelly gas, coming up from below. On a later podcast episode he holds up the paper and reads its full title, which speaks of acid-formed deposits in cave layers and of hydrocarbon gas seeping up at Giza. So the two tellings differ slightly on which gas is the focus. He tells it because, in his view, gas rising beneath the pyramids would support the idea that they were built to do something with energy.
